correctness.rationale: Negating X in Q reduces the test to f_c and f_−c. Independently checked the cubic discriminant −t²(3t²−14t+27), the derivative of −X³/(X²+X+1) and the quadratic resultant 63504. For p≥11 the poles are simple; the geometric inertia types are a 3-cycle at 0 and transpositions at the two simple discriminant roots for each cover. Each cover is connected with S3 closure. The two quadratic discriminant square classes differ at their disjoint simple roots, so the two geometric closures have trivial intersection: any nontrivial common S3 quotient would have the quadratic quotient. The arithmetic action embeds in S3×S3 and already contains the geometric product, so there is no constant extension. Tame inertia in the compositum is cyclic, of order three at the common branch point and two at the four remaining ones. Riemann–Hurwitz gives genus 13; the twist fiber on an unramified rational base point contributes either zero or the centralizer size nine, since irreducibility is the 3-cycle class in each coordinate. No finite ramified parameter qualifies. At most 12+4·18+9=93 extra points can lie over the exceptional parameters including infinity, giving the claimed estimate by Weil. For p≥851, p+1−26√p−93 is increasing and positive already at 851 (759²>676·851). A separately written direct-root test of both polynomials, not the uploaded rational-map sieve, exhausted all 146 primes through 850 and returned exactly 2,3,5,13 as the zero counts. Opposite parameters then give pairs for all remaining odd primes. The bound is proved for p≥11 only, and no extension-field classification is asserted.
